newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London on standby, await jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London on standby, await jobs data.

text.p: U.S. shares were at a virtual standstill in Europe on Friday as investors waited for key U.S. unemployment figures, due at 1330 GMT/0830 EST.
"It has been very quiet indeed. Nothing much is going to happen until the U.S. numbers," one market maker said.
The key non-farm payroll total is forecast to rise by 237,000 in January, according to a Reuters poll of economists. Average hourly earnings for the month are seen rising by 0.2 percent.
Dealers fear stronger-than-expected figures could send both bond and equities markets lower.
Only a handful of shares had traded by 1100 GMT.

American Express was up $1/2 at $62-1/2 following press reports that the U.S. Justice Department was preparing to file an anti-trust suit against VISA USA and MasterCard International for barring member banks from issuing AMEX and Discover credit cards.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday that the suit could be filed as early as the end of the month unless VISA and MasterCard agreed to change their rules.
Elsewhere, IBM, which dropped $2-3/4 in New York on Thursday, was up $3/8 at $146.
Intel rose $1/2 to $153-5/8 after losing $4-1/8 overnight.
The March T-bond was up 1/32 at 111-30/32 while the cash 30-year long bond was trading at 96.20, yielding 6.76 percent.
